---
title: "Tuning of the logistic (non-linear) DGM"
format: html
editor: visual
---

Parameters of the non-linear DGM defined in `shape_logistic.qmd`, chosen so that the populations have the same properties as in the linear branch:

1.  **treatment model**: SMDs of 0.5 for age of onset and sex between treated and historical controls (as in `tune.qmd`; the treatment model does not depend on the HUI, so these values are the same as in the linear branch);
2.  **drift**: year of onset changes the HUI by about 0.005 per year, as in the linear DGM;
3.  **confounding**: the difference in untreated HUI at 2 years between treated and controls due to age of onset and sex is $-0.02$, the target of the linear tuning ($-0.20\times0.10$), half from each covariate;
4.  **treatment effects**: the true effect on the HUI scale at 2 years among the treated (treated minus untreated HUI) is 0, 0.05, 0.15 and 0.30, as in the linear branch.

The steps are done in this order because each depends on the previous one: on a bounded scale the same latent coefficient gives a different effect depending on where patients are on the curve. Everything is computed at the patient level at the landmark (2 years after onset = 2 years after the start of treatment in the anchored branch), on a large population.

# Libraries

```{r}
pacman::p_load(dplyr,lubridate)
```

# Settings

```{r}
source("C:\\Users\\P095206\\OneDrive - Amsterdam UMC\\Shared material with Elia\\PhD\\Project 5 - Simulation study in SATs\\Code\\paper\\R\\functions\\wrapper\\continuous\\without duration\\rtruncexp.R")
# shape, as chosen in shape_logistic.qmd
expit=function(x) 1/(1+exp(-x)); logit=function(p) log(p/(1-p))
L=-0.36; U=1
hui=function(eta) L+(U-L)*expit(eta)
eta_of=function(h) logit((h-L)/(U-L))
hui_onset=0.85; hui_ref=0; t_ref=5
a0=eta_of(hui_onset)
k=(eta_of(hui_onset)-eta_of(hui_ref))/t_ref
sd_u0=0.5; sd_eps=0.3
# targets, as in the linear branch
target_smd_age=0.5; target_smd_sex=0.5; t_int=-1
target_bias=-0.20*0.10; share_age=0.5
drift_hui=0.005
targets=c(0,0.025,0.075,0.15)*2     # true effects at the landmark: 0, 0.05, 0.15, 0.30
landmark=2
trialdate=as.Date("2021-05-31")
n=1e6
```

# Population

Patients at onset, with the covariates of the main DGM, the random intercept and the measurement error at the landmark visit.

```{r}
set.seed(3111963)
end_date=as.Date("2022-12-31")
pop=tibble(dateonset=end_date-floor(rtruncexp(n=n,rate=0.0002,max=as.numeric(end_date-as.Date("2005-01-01")))),
           aoo=runif(n,0,8),
           male=as.integer(runif(n)<0.5),
           u=runif(n),
           u0=rnorm(n,0,sd_u0),
           eps=rnorm(n,0,sd_eps)) %>%
  mutate(yoo=year(dateonset),
         yoo_c=yoo-mean(yoo),
         post=dateonset>=trialdate)
smd_abs=function(x,g) abs((mean(x[g==1])-mean(x[g==0]))/sqrt((var(x[g==1])+var(x[g==0]))/2))
```

# 1. Treatment model: SMDs

Treated: onset after the trial date and treated according to the treatment model; historical controls: onset before the trial date (untreated patients with onset after the trial date are excluded).

```{r}
select_trt=function(d,t_age,t_sex){
  d %>% mutate(trt=as.integer(u<plogis(t_int-t_age*aoo+t_sex*male) & post)) %>%
    filter(trt==1 | !post)
}
obj=function(par){
  d=select_trt(pop,par[1],par[2])
  (smd_abs(d$aoo,d$trt)-target_smd_age)^2+(smd_abs(d$male,d$trt)-target_smd_sex)^2
}
o=optim(c(0.3,1.4),obj,method="Nelder-Mead",control=list(reltol=1e-10))
t_age=o$par[1]; t_sex=o$par[2]
d=select_trt(pop,t_age,t_sex)
c(t_int=t_int,t_age=t_age,t_sex=t_sex,smd_age=smd_abs(d$aoo,d$trt),smd_sex=smd_abs(d$male,d$trt),
  treated=sum(d$trt),controls=sum(1-d$trt))
```

# 2. Drift

The latent effect of year of onset that changes the HUI by about `drift_hui` per year at the landmark, on average: $\beta_{yoo}=$ `drift_hui` / mean of $dHUI/d\eta$.

```{r}
eta_landmark=function(d,b_aoo,b_male,b_yoo,gamma=0){
  a0+d$u0+b_aoo*(d$aoo-mean(pop$aoo))+b_male*(d$male-mean(pop$male))+b_yoo*d$yoo_c-k*landmark+gamma*landmark*d$trt+d$eps
}
slope=function(eta) (U-L)*expit(eta)*(1-expit(eta))
b_yoo=drift_hui/mean(slope(eta_landmark(d,0,0,0)))
b_yoo
```

# 3. Confounding: covariate effects

The covariate effects are scaled together by $s$: age of onset and sex each account for half of the latent difference between treated and controls ($\beta_{aoo}\,\Delta_{aoo}=\beta_{male}\,\Delta_{male}=s/2$). $s$ is found so that the difference in untreated HUI at the landmark due to these covariates (drift excluded, as in the linear tuning) equals `target_bias`.

```{r}
diff_aoo=mean(d$aoo[d$trt==1])-mean(d$aoo[d$trt==0])
diff_male=mean(d$male[d$trt==1])-mean(d$male[d$trt==0])
coefs=function(s) c(b_aoo=share_age*s/diff_aoo,b_male=(1-share_age)*s/diff_male)
bias_hui=function(s){
  b=coefs(s)
  h0=hui(eta_landmark(d,b["b_aoo"],b["b_male"],0))
  mean(h0[d$trt==1])-mean(h0[d$trt==0])
}
s=uniroot(function(s) bias_hui(s)-target_bias,c(-3,3),tol=1e-10)$root
b=coefs(s)
c(s=s,b,bias=bias_hui(s))
```

# 4. Treatment effects

True effect at the landmark among the treated: mean of the treated minus the untreated HUI of the same patients (same random intercept and measurement error). $\gamma$ is found for every target; the largest effect that is possible on a bounded scale ($\gamma\to\infty$, every treated patient at the ceiling) is shown as a check.

```{r}
tr=d %>% filter(trt==1)
h0=hui(eta_landmark(tr,b["b_aoo"],b["b_male"],b_yoo))
effect=function(gamma) mean(hui(eta_landmark(tr,b["b_aoo"],b["b_male"],b_yoo,gamma))-h0)
max_effect=mean(U-h0)
gammas=sapply(targets,function(target) if (target==0) 0 else uniroot(function(g) effect(g)-target,c(0,20),tol=1e-10)$root)
tibble(true_effect=targets,gamma=gammas,delta=gammas/k,check=sapply(gammas,effect))
c(mean_untreated_hui_treated_at_landmark=mean(h0),max_possible_effect=max_effect)
```

# Parameters for the non-linear DGM

To copy into the non-linear version of `effect_size_loop`.

```{r}
params=c(a0=a0,k=k,sd_u0=sd_u0,sd_eps=sd_eps,
         t_int=t_int,t_age=t_age,t_sex=t_sex,
         b_aoo=unname(b["b_aoo"]),b_male=unname(b["b_male"]),b_yoo=b_yoo,
         setNames(gammas,paste0("gamma_",targets)))
round(params,4)
cat(paste0("aoo_mean=",round(mean(pop$aoo),4),"; male_mean=",round(mean(pop$male),4),
           " # centring values used for the covariates\n"))
```
